title: DC-area forecast: Heat is back for now, and storm chances return Thursday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Following above average highs in the upper 80s to near 90, we're mostly clear this evening with only a slow dip backwards through the 80s.

What’s next? More humid tomorrow with a chance for scattered showers and storms. Friday should be dry and a bit cooler. Some showers and a storm are possible this weekend, perhaps more so on Saturday than Sunday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Skies stay mostly clear as we hang on to a breeze from the south and southwest. Humidity creeps a bit higher with lows in the upper 60s to mid-70s. Confidence: High

Tomorrow (Thursday): Partly sunny with highs in the mid-80s to near 90. Higher humidity (dew points in the mid-60s to near 70) push the heat index deep into the 90s. A few showers are possible in the morning, then we could see scattered showers and storms late afternoon or evening as a cold front approaches from the northwest. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Mostly cloudy and rather muggy with the chance for scattered showers, maybe a thunderstorm, during the evening and overnight as the cold front pushes through. Lows in the upper 60s to near 70. Confidence: Low-Medium

A look ahead

Friday starts mostly cloudy and still on the humid side. But skies should gradually brighten as the cold front pushes farther away to our south, and the humidity should eventually come down a bit. Cooler highs top out in the upper 70s to low 80s. Partly cloudy Friday night with lows in the 60s. Confidence: Medium

Partly to mostly cloudy Saturday with some showers and a thunderstorm possible at some point Saturday into Saturday night. Daytime highs reach the mid-70s to low 80s as humidity trends back higher again. Saturday night lows settle in the mid-60s to low 70s. Confidence: Low

We may hang on to the chance of an isolated shower or storm on Sunday, when skies should be partly sunny with highs in the upper 70s to mid-80s. Confidence: Low-Medium

DC weather history for September 9

A 2018 rainstorm set a daily record and contributed to one of the wettest years on record, with an unusually high number of days topping an inch of rainfall.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Some spots have a shot at 90 degrees. But September heat isn't as harsh as midsummer, and humidity is still relatively tame. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
